# July 4th, 2026

*at \~6 PM PST*



<br>



To my American visitors, happy 4th of July, and happy 250th birthday to this country!

I am not going to lie; it’s been somewhat refreshing to see the influx of international soccer/football fans and to hear kind things from them about my country for once. It’s been a nice reminder that the plights of the average American are with their government, not their next-door neighbor. It’s still possible to align deeply with your countrymen, even if we do not always agree on what the best path forward may be. The camaraderie of everyday people and overarching sense of community we share is vastly more important than the words of any politician; and I believe it is very much okay to take pride in each other.



At any rate, this won’t be a terribly long post; I mainly want to put something here to catch up and so that the website doesn’t appear abandoned. How are you all doing? I’ve been alright myself, just working and enjoying life to the best of my ability.



<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="" style="width: 40cqi" /><br>*A beautiful F-22 Raptor I saw while visiting a friend in Utah this past May*



I went to Utah back in May with some buddies to visit a friend and had the absolute time of my life, if I’m honest. Between dancing with a pretty girl (poorly) for the first time, visiting a military aviation museum, going camping, and shooting a Barret .50cal and my M1911, I’ve absolutely had my fill.

You know the trip went well when you find yourself daydreaming about staying behind and starting a new life there. Some parts of Utah are pretty gorgeous, I can’t lie.



Also, I recently got my beloved KTM 390 Adv back from a 15k mile valve clearance adjustment and new rear tire installation. Am looking forward to taking long rides and rejoining my fellow two-wheel enthusiasts on the open road. I’ve needed it for some time.



<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="" style="width: 40cqi" /><br>*White Forest – as seen in Half-Life 2: Episode 2*



Beyond these things, I’ve also played Half-Life 1 \& 2 to completion since the start of this year. I must commend Valve on their ability to write characters and create a story that you can immerse yourself in. Similar to the lively characters of Azumanga Daioh, I find myself wishing that the characters of the Half-Life universe were real people. Eli Vance seems like he’d have been a hell of a guy to have a few beers with and just exchange stories. Is it weird to personify these characters in such a way? If I were a writer for HL, I’d take these statements as compliments more than anything.



With all that said, I think I've just about summed up the past couple months well enough. Am looking forward to continuing development on this website and furthering my still-pretty-hazy vision. Take care!
